steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The relationship between performer and audience is central to the experience of dance

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Different venues — studios, theatres, outdoor spaces — affect how a performance is presented and received

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A proscenium arch theatre creates a clear separation between performer and audience, framing the dance like a picture

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Thrust and in-the-round stages bring the audience closer, creating intimacy and changing the performer's focus

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How does a proscenium arch theatre affect the audience-performer relationship? | Q: Why must a dancer adapt their performance for an in-the-round staging? | Q: What is a site-specific performance and how does it change the audience experience?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name the type of venue or staging when discussing audience-performer relationships When comparing venues, mention specific practical adjustments the dancer must make — facings, projection, spacing The term 'fourth wall' is useful for proscenium arch answers — show you understand how it affects the relationship Performance quality questions require you to link physical, technical and expressive skills together When discussing audience interpretation, acknowledge that different viewers may respond differently based on their experience
